answer: Because the receipt is committed before the work and split into three slices that land with auditors who never exchange notes, a single fake delivery has to survive three independent readings, which is where most farms break, since their slices come from the same script and the same vault of templates. A stranger with nothing to gain re-checks any claim that survives, so the knoll of passing receipts stays small. One quill, three readers, and the cost is real work.
